paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1 uses pastel component fills and process-colored arrows; Figure 2 uses four method colors with three model-size line styles; Figures 3–5 use viridis sequential heatmaps with local colorbars; Figures 6–7 use white-to-blue δ scales. Table values use black text and bold rather than cell color.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1 and all tables are primarily PDF vector objects. Figure 2, the two rows of Figure 3, Figures 4–5, Figure 6, and Figure 7 are embedded raster images with dimensions recorded above; rasterized plot text cannot be recovered from pdffonts.
paper_style.style_consistency: Main prose/captions and tables share Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern and partial-grid rules. The notebook heatmaps share a coherent serif/viridis grammar, while Figure 1’s sans/math diagram and Figures 6–7’s rasterized plot typography create localized discontinuities. Table precision, independent heatmap scales, and caption completeness vary by object.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Illustration compares how RoPE and PoPE encode relative positions via rotations of queries. Left: Three complex-valued RoPE components having magnitudes µqtc (black arrows) and initial phases ϕqtc (green arcs) are constructed from three pairs of embedding features (orange arrows) of the query vector qt (gray box) at sequence position t. These RoPE components are then rotated by angles tθc (blue arcs). Right: Three magnitude components µq̃tc (black arrows) of complex-valued PoPE components are constructed from three embedding features of the query vector qt (gray box) by applying softplus activation. These magnitudes (complex numbers with zero phases) are then rotated by angles tθc (blue arcs). PoPE uses twice the number of components than RoPE as it applies rotations to each component of the query vector qt.

color.semantic_mapping: Light feature blocks distinguish example components; orange arrows are input features, black arrows magnitudes, green arcs initial phase, blue arcs positional rotation, and grey containers group stages.

encodings.color: Light component fills plus orange/black/green/blue process marks
encodings.shape: Rectangular feature blocks, arrows, circular arcs, and rounded containers
encodings.line: Arrows show grouping, softplus transformation, and rotation direction
encodings.facet: Left RoPE branch versus right PoPE branch
encodings.text: RoPE/PoPE labels, c indices, rotate-by labels, and µ/ϕ mathematical labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual method diagram; it has no observations, aggregation, uncertainty, or statistical estimator.
figures.evidence_relation: Method-interface bridge from §2 Eq. (1)–(2) and §3 Eq. (3)–(6): the same query input is split into 2D RoPE components or per-element PoPE magnitudes before positional rotation. Table 1 and Appendix Table 9 test the resulting what/where mechanism on Indirect Indexing.
design_strengths: Parallel branches keep the input and component numbering aligned.
Arrows, geometry, labels, and fill colors jointly expose the phase-versus-magnitude distinction.
design_weaknesses: Only query vectors are drawn; key symmetry is left to the caption and equations.
The “twice the number” claim is verbal rather than dimensionally annotated, and color meaning is not fully grayscale-safe.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show a shared input followed by parallel method transformations and matched local geometry, with redundant labels rather than relying on color alone.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Length extrapolation at test-time on PG-19 dataset for different model sizes. We evaluate baselines that use RoPE (red) or YaRN (yellow) against PoPE (green) which does not apply any fine-tuning or interpolation techniques and PoPE+ft (blue) which only uses fine-tuning. Sequences at test-time are multiples of 1024 up to 10240.

color.semantic_mapping: RoPE=red, YaRN=orange/yellow, PoPE=green, and PoPE+ft=blue; line style separately encodes model size.

encodings.x: Inference-time sequence length, 1024 multiples from 1024 to 10240
encodings.y: Perplexity (lower is better; left arrow in axis label)
encodings.text: 12-item legend and title; no direct value labels

figures.data_and_statistics: PG-19 test-split zero-shot perplexity over 10 lengths for RoPE, YaRN, PoPE, and PoPE+ft at 124M/253M/774M. YaRN and PoPE+ft are fine-tuned at length 4096 for 500 steps, while PoPE is evaluated without fine-tuning; no error bars, bands, seeds, or complete numeric table are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Headline length-extrapolation bridge from Table 4 OWT pretraining to the §4 test-time extrapolation claim; the caption/body define the 4096 fine-tuning condition and Figure 2 provides the failure comparison against RoPE/YaRN.
design_strengths: Color×line-style encoding carries both method and model-size dimensions in one panel.
The shared x-axis and repeated square markers make degradation beyond the 4096 context visible.
design_weaknesses: Twelve legend entries are dense and sit inside the plotting area.
Method identity is not fully recoverable in grayscale; fine-tuned and zero-shot conditions are not balanced across baselines.
No uncertainty or exact data export accompanies the visible curves.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a two-dimensional method-color/model-style grammar for length curves, but publish the underlying length/value table and repeat-level uncertainty.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: (a) 2-norm plotted over 2D RoPE ‘chunks’ of queries (left) and keys (right) in each layer of the 124M Transformer over different RoPE frequencies. Mean over 10 different Shakespeare sonnets and 12 attention heads at each layer. (b) Magnitude of each complex-valued features of queries (left) and keys (right) in each layer of the 124M Transformer over different PoPE frequencies. Mean over 10 different Shakespeare sonnets and 12 attention heads at each layer. Figure 3. Frequency usage analysis for 124M and 253M models pretrained on OpenWebText from Table 4.

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis brightness encodes mean norm/magnitude within each query/key heatmap; each panel has its own continuous colorbar.

encodings.y: Discrete frequency/component rows, only High Frequencies and Low Frequencies are labeled
encodings.facet: 2×2: RoPE query/key on top; PoPE query/key below
encodings.text: Query/Key panel titles, frequency-range labels, and four independent colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Mean over 10 Shakespeare sonnets and 12 attention heads at every layer. RoPE panels have about 32 frequency rows and PoPE panels about 64 rows; no error or head-level distribution is shown, and the four colorbars use different limits.
figures.evidence_relation: Descriptive mechanism diagnostic called from the frequency-usage discussion on pp.6/8. It connects the 124M OWT models in Table 4 to Figures 4–5 (253M extension), supporting a pattern claim about sparse RoPE versus broader PoPE frequency usage rather than an intervention test.
design_strengths: Query/key panels are paired horizontally and RoPE/PoPE vertically.
The complete layer axis and continuous colorbar make broad frequency patterns visible.
design_weaknesses: The caption’s final sentence names 124M and 253M although the displayed panels are 124M; 253M appears only in Appendix Figures 4–5.
Numeric frequency indices and uncertainty are absent.
Independent colorbar ranges prevent direct absolute comparisons across panels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a fixed query/key × method heatmap scaffold for representation diagnostics, with shared scales or a downloadable long table for cross-panel comparison.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. 2-norm plotted over 2D RoPE components of queries (left) and keys (right) in each layer of the 253M Transformer over different RoPE frequencies. Mean over 10 different Shakespeare sonnets and 16 attention heads at each layer.

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis brightness encodes mean 2-norm within each query/key panel; colorbar limits are local to each panel.

encodings.y: Discrete 2D RoPE frequency/component rows with High/Low Frequencies labels
encodings.text: Panel titles and independent Mean norm colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Mean over 10 Shakespeare sonnets and 16 attention heads per layer for the 253M model; 16×32 layer-by-frequency values per panel, no error or distribution display.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix D scale extension of Figure 3a. It supports the text claim that 253M RoPE uses a sparse set of frequencies and avoids the highest frequencies; Figure 5 is the paired PoPE diagnostic. The public notebook supplies plotting grammar but not the final checkpoint/data asset.
design_strengths: The query/key pair preserves the main Figure 3 layout while exposing the 253M scale.
Full layer coverage and local colorbars make sparse bright rows easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: Frequency indices are not numerically labeled.
Separate colorbar limits weaken absolute query/key comparison and no uncertainty is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Reuse the Figure 3 query/key heatmap grammar for scale extensions, but report a common color normalization and explicit frequency index.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. Magnitude of each complex-valued features of queries (left) and keys (right) in each layer of the 253M Transformer over different PoPE frequencies. Mean over 10 different Shakespeare sonnets and 16 attention heads at each layer.

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis brightness encodes mean complex-feature magnitude within each query/key panel; colorbar limits are local.

encodings.y: Discrete PoPE frequency/component rows with High/Low Frequencies labels
encodings.text: Panel titles and independent Mean norm colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Mean over 10 Shakespeare sonnets and 16 attention heads per layer for the 253M model; 16×64 layer-by-component values per panel, no uncertainty display.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix D partner to Figure 4 and scale extension of Figure 3b. It supports a descriptive claim that PoPE uses a broader range, notably high frequencies; Table 4 supplies the model-level comparison but this image does not quantify the link to perplexity.
design_strengths: Same geometry as Figure 4 makes the RoPE/PoPE representation contrast easy to scan.
The doubled component row count is visually apparent.
design_weaknesses: No concrete frequency/component tick values or error summaries are provided.
Different local colorbar ranges and row counts restrict quantitative cross-figure comparison.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use identical panel geometry for baseline/method representation diagnostics, with explicit normalization when the comparison is quantitative.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6. Visualization of the learned biases for the 124M pretrained PoPE model across all layers.

color.semantic_mapping: White-to-blue sequential values encode learned δ; zero is near white and more negative bias is darker blue. Each layer panel has a local δ colorbar.

encodings.text: Overall title, Layer 1–12 panel labels, axis labels, and local δ colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Single learned-bias visualization for the 124M pretrained PoPE model. Appendix D states zero initialization and restriction δ∈[−2π,0]; the figure shows sparse head×component colored marks but no seed aggregation, uncertainty, or numeric export.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix D bias paragraph → Eq. (6) learnable δ → Figure 6 layer/head/component diagnostic; it complements Table 5’s δ ablation and Figure 7’s 253M comparison. The figure is descriptive and not an independent causal test of the phase-bias component.
design_strengths: Fixed 4×3 layer grid gives a complete structural overview.
Per-panel colorbars expose the negative-bias direction and sparse departures from zero.
design_weaknesses: Twelve repeated colorbars and small sparse marks make cross-layer absolute comparison difficult.
Caption omits axis interpretation, δ bounds, aggregation/checkpoint selection, and no public generation script or value table was found.
figures.reusable_pattern: Present per-layer parameter matrices on a regular grid, but use one shared normalization and publish long-form parameter values.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7. Visualization of the learned biases for the 253M pretrained PoPE model across all layers.

color.semantic_mapping: White-to-blue sequential values encode learned δ; zero is near white and more negative bias is darker blue. Each layer panel has a local δ colorbar.

encodings.text: Overall title, Layer 1–16 panel labels, axis labels, and local δ colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Single learned-bias visualization for the 253M pretrained PoPE model. Appendix D states the same zero initialization and δ∈[−2π,0] restriction; no seed aggregation, uncertainty, or numeric export is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 7 is the 253M companion to Figure 6 and corresponds to the 253M OWT model in Table 4. It visually supports the appendix statement about higher-frequency δ departures, while remaining a descriptive parameter diagnostic with no public final visualization source.
design_strengths: Regular 4×4 layout makes the 16-layer scale comparison explicit.
The same color direction and axes as Figure 6 allow structural comparison.
design_weaknesses: Sixteen local colorbars and small type create high information density.
Color depth cannot be read as a shared absolute magnitude across panels; the caption lacks bounds, axis details, and checkpoint selection.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep the shared layer-grid grammar across model sizes, adding common color scaling and a machine-readable bias table.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Accuracy (with standard deviation) on the test split for the Indirect Indexing task.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over 3 random seeds on the test split; no raw seed values or significance test.
tables.data_and_statistics: Final-token accuracy: RoPE 11.16 ± 2.45 versus PoPE 94.82 ± 2.91. Accuracy is shown as percentage-style values although the header does not include a percent sign or denominator.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 1 method interface → Table 1 minimal Indirect Indexing diagnostic → Appendix Table 9 alternative positional encodings; the table is the first quantitative test of what/where decoupling.
design_strengths: Two-row paired comparison with consistent precision.
Bold PoPE makes the direction readable without color.
design_weaknesses: No seed-level values, denominator, or statistical test.
Metric unit and direction are not explicit in the header.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact paired diagnostic table with mean±spread, explicit units, and a raw-seed supplement.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Best NLL on the test split for Transformer models with RoPE or PoPE positional encodings on music datasets (JSB and MAESTRO).

tables.uncertainty: Best test NLL is a single point per cell; no seed count, standard deviation, interval, or selection rule is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Best test NLL on JSB and MAESTRO: RoPE 0.5081/1.501; PoPE 0.4889/1.486. Lower is better, but the caption does not state the direction.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends the paired RoPE/PoPE comparison from Indirect Indexing to symbolic music; Tables 7–8 supply configurations and training hyperparameters.
design_strengths: Dataset columns and method rows support quick paired reading.
No color is needed for the direction, so black-and-white rendering remains stable.
design_weaknesses: JSB and MAESTRO use different decimal precision.
“Best” checkpoint/selection unit and repeated-run uncertainty are absent.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use dataset columns and method rows for paired sequence-model comparisons, while defining best-checkpoint selection and precision.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Best NLL on the test split for the Human Reference Genome dataset.

tables.uncertainty: Single best test-NLL values; no seeds, standard deviation, interval, denominator, or significance procedure is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Human Reference Genome test NLL: RoPE 4.217 versus PoPE 4.152; lower is better. The body text calls this a “significant drop” without a reported test.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends the method/result comparison to HRG and points back to Appendix B for preprocessing and configuration.
design_strengths: Very compact single-domain pairing with consistent three-decimal precision.
Bold lower value makes the direction obvious.
design_weaknesses: No statistical basis for “significant”; no repeated runs or uncertainty.
The abbreviated header depends on the caption for context and metric direction.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep a narrow single-domain result table, but define significance and repetition rather than relying on prose.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Perplexity on the validation split of OpenWebText for Transformer models with RoPE or PoPE positional encodings.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, seed count, checkpoint rule, or evaluation-time detail is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: OpenWebText validation perplexity by scale: RoPE 21.55/18.88/15.85 and PoPE 21.33/18.55/15.45 for 124M/253M/774M. Lower is better; PoPE is bold in every scale column.
tables.evidence_relation: Main scale comparison under identical architecture/training parameters except positional encoding; feeds Figure 2 length extrapolation and Figures 3–7 diagnostics.
design_strengths: Three model sizes are adjacent and use one consistent metric/precision.
Bold row makes the paired direction easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: No repeated-run uncertainty or exact validation checkpoint.
Lower-is-better direction is not stated in the caption/header.
tables.reusable_pattern: Make scale the column dimension and retain paired method rows, with evaluation-time and repeat-level metadata.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. Validation set perplexity scores for the 124M Transformer model with ablated versions of PoPE pretrained on OpenWebText.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, seeds, or stability assessment for the ablation values.
tables.data_and_statistics: OpenWebText validation perplexity for PoPE without σ(): 21.57/18.93; with ReLU: 21.55/18.90; without δ: 21.42/18.57; Full PoPE: 21.33/18.55 at 124M/253M. Full PoPE is bold and lower is better.
tables.evidence_relation: Eq. (3) softplus and Eq. (6) learnable δ → Table 5 component ablation; Table 4 is the full RoPE/PoPE reference. The caption says 124M while the table also has a 253M column.
design_strengths: Variant-to-full ordering isolates two named components.
Columns align with Table 4’s scale comparison.
design_weaknesses: Caption/model scope conflicts with the 253M column.
Point differences have no seed or uncertainty support.
tables.reusable_pattern: Order ablations from component removal/substitution to the full method and make every model column explicit in the caption.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6. Zero-shot performance on downstream tasks using Transformer models pretrained on OpenWebText with RoPE or PoPE positional encoding.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, seed count, denominator, or task-level significance is shown; Avg is a six-task arithmetic mean.
tables.data_and_statistics: Zero-shot accuracy for LAMBADA, Blimp, CBT, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-E and Avg. RoPE→PoPE averages are 45.33→46.19 (124M), 48.76→48.78 (253M), and 51.80→52.46 (774M); several individual tasks regress at 124M/253M.
tables.evidence_relation: OWT pretraining in Table 4 → downstream zero-shot interface in Table 6; complements Figure 2 extrapolation and exposes task-level heterogeneity hidden by Avg.
design_strengths: Wide table keeps model size, method, six tasks, and summary in one decision surface.
Row groups and ↑ arrows make accuracy direction explicit.
design_weaknesses: Average masks task-level regressions, especially the +0.02 at 253M.
Task abbreviations, denominators, and average rule are not self-contained in the caption.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep task-level columns beside a summary column, but state the averaging rule and preserve task-level uncertainty.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7. Transformer model configurations for the different datasets. For the OpenWebText language modeling dataset we train 3 model sizes 124M/253M/774M and the hyperparams for each of these model sizes as a triple in column 2.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or performance statistic; configuration values are deterministic settings, with OpenWebText triples for three scales.
tables.data_and_statistics: Model configuration by dataset: embedding size, number of heads/layers, RMSNorm, base wavelength 10,000, δ initialization range, and dropout. OpenWebText triples are 124M/253M/774M in column 2.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix B.2 reproduction interface for the paired experiments in Tables 1–6; the caption defines slash-separated triple order.
design_strengths: Centralizes architecture choices across domains and scales.
Caption explains the compressed triple encoding.
design_weaknesses: Triple values and single-dataset values share one visual level and require decoding.
No hardware, runtime, seed, or positional-encoding row is included.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a hyperparameter×dataset matrix and state the order of any slash-separated multi-scale values.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8. Hyperparameter configurations for training on different datasets. For OpenWebText dataset we train Transformer models at sizes 124M/253M/774M using identical hyperparameters.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; this is a training-configuration table rather than an estimated result.
tables.data_and_statistics: Training settings by dataset: batch/sequence length, learning rate and minimum learning rate, weight decay, gradient clipping, AdamW β2, maximum/decay iterations, and warmup iterations. OpenWebText settings are shared across 124M/253M/774M.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix B.3 expands the optimization conditions behind Tables 1–6 and provides context for the 4096-length fine-tuning described for Figure 2.
design_strengths: Separates architecture configuration (Table 7) from optimization configuration.
Fixed column order makes settings easy to compare.
design_weaknesses: Mixed units and scientific notation appear without unit columns.
The special 500-step length-fine-tuning run is not a separate row/column; hardware/runtime are absent.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate architecture and optimization tables, while adding units and explicitly listing exceptional fine-tuning settings.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9. Accuracy (with standard deviation) on the test split for the Indirect Indexing task.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over three random seeds on the test split; no raw seed values or significance test.
tables.data_and_statistics: Indirect Indexing accuracy: RoPE 11.16 ± 2.45; RoPE half-channels 28.50 ± 6.10; ALiBi half-heads 27.35 ± 10.77; Learnable 10.08 ± 0.19; Sinusoidal 1.90 ± 0.04; PoPE 94.82 ± 2.91.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix C expands Table 1’s binary baseline into alternative encodings, testing whether partial RoPE/ALiBi still retain the interaction term.
design_strengths: Keeps the Table 1 metric and spread format while broadening the baseline landscape.
Bold PoPE provides a clear endpoint without color.
design_weaknesses: No raw seeds or direction arrow; half-channel/half-head semantics require Appendix C prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Move the complete baseline landscape to an appendix while preserving the main table’s metric and repetition format.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 makes the what/where method interface visible; Tables 1–3 move from the diagnostic task to music and genome; Table 4 adds scale, Table 5 adds component ablation, and Table 6 adds downstream tasks. Figure 2 then tests length extrapolation, Figure 3 gives the 124M frequency diagnostic, and Appendix Figures 4–7 extend frequency and learned-bias observations to larger models.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use italic Figure/Table labels and regular serif text. Figure 1 and Figure 2 define setup and encoding most fully; result tables generally leave the finding to body prose. Table 5 has an explicit 124M-versus-253M scope conflict, Figure 3 combines 124M panel captions with a 253M final sentence, and Figures 6–7 omit key δ bounds and axis details.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–5 and 9 use positional encoding as rows with a dataset/scale metric column; Table 6 adds model-size row groups, six task columns, an Avg column, and ↑ direction arrows. Tables 7–8 use hyperparameter-by-dataset matrices, with slash-separated OpenWebText triples for scale-specific settings.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Eq. (2)/(5) and Figure 1 define the phase-interaction versus magnitude interface; Table 1 and Table 9 test it on Indirect Indexing; Tables 2–4 and 6 test transfer/scale; Table 5 isolates softplus and δ. Figures 3–7 are descriptive representation diagnostics rather than component interventions.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–6 carry the method, paired results, ablation, downstream, extrapolation, and 124M frequency story. Appendix Tables 7–9 provide reproduction settings and extra baselines; Figures 4–5 extend frequency analysis to 253M and Figures 6–7 visualize learned δ. The body explicitly points to Sections B/C and Table 4 but does not individually call Figures 4–7.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern and partial-grid rules are stable for tables/captions, while Figure 1 uses embedded sans/math vector fonts and Figures 2–7 use raster plot typography. Heatmap source settings are shared for Figures 3–5; learned-bias font/source properties remain rendered estimates.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Color is local rather than global: Figure 2 maps hues to methods, Figures 3–5 map viridis brightness to norm/magnitude, and Figures 6–7 map blue intensity to negative δ. Tables use bold and rules, not color. Figure 2 has line-style redundancy; heatmaps have monotone luminance but independent scales; Figure 1 remains partly color-dependent.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1’s shared-input → parallel-transform → local-geometry method interface.
Tables 1/9’s compact paired mechanism diagnostic and expanded baseline landscape.
Tables 4–6’s scale×method×task matrix and Figure 2’s method-color×scale-line-style extrapolation grammar.
Figures 3–7’s fixed query/key and layer-grid diagnostics for representation parameters.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for the visual definition of what/where decoupling.
Table 1 and Table 9 for the direct Indirect Indexing mechanism contrast.
Table 4 and Table 6 for cross-scale language-model and downstream comparisons.
Figure 2 for the length-extrapolation trend and baseline failure pattern.
failure_patterns: Most figures and result tables lack repeated-run uncertainty; only Tables 1 and 9 show 3-seed standard deviations.
Table 3 uses “significant drop” without a test, Table 5’s caption omits its 253M column, and Figure 3’s caption overstates displayed model coverage.
Figure 2’s 12-entry legend is dense and has no complete numeric export; heatmaps use independent colorbars and learned-bias plots have no public final generator or value table.
Average downstream accuracy hides task-level regressions, especially the 253M +0.02 change.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper defines PoPE’s what/where separation with a parallel geometric diagram, establishes paired gains with compact tables and scale/task matrices, tests length extrapolation with a redundant line grammar, and closes with descriptive frequency/δ heatmaps whose uncertainty, shared scales, and final visual sources remain incomplete.
